MAJOR: Delta replaces the explicit project-first rule in `scripts/dev/backlog_db_parity.py` (`d.get("project") or d.get("scope")`) with `db_tenant(d.get("scope"), d.get("project"))`, but adds no test asserting the canonical `_db_tenant` preserves project-over-scope priority when an item carries both fields. AC-3's `parity.txt` is produced by this exact path, so a silent re-resolve changes tenant bucketing and invalidates the parity/backfill evidence without failing the command.
MINOR: `from core.backlog import db_tenant` imports the env/DB-sensitive core module (whose `PF_BACKLOG_DB` default is now `on`) into a read-only parity tool at import time, coupling file-side parity computation to import-time side effects and DB/edpsvc availability.

The delta chooses `core.backlog.db_tenant` as the resolver, while `engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1531/current-sha-control.txt` still names `core/backlog_scope.py` as the single scope-resolver owner; code and control evidence now point at different owners.
No test in the delta asserts `db_tenant` is the sole owner (i.e., that no other copy of the scope/legacy-alias mapping remains), so the SSOT regression the prior MAJOR identified can recur unnoticed.
NIT: `sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))` is unconditional and top-precedence with no guard, so importing the script as a module would silently reorder `sys.path[0]` instead of only running the tool.
`from core.backlog import db_tenant` is placed after non-import statements (`ROOT = ...`, `sys.path.insert`) rather than the import block (E402), a side effect of the path shim.

`db_tenant` in `core/backlog.py` is a pure one-line delegation with no docstring pointer to the underlying `_db_tenant` rules (project-vs-scope priority, legacy `factory` alias), leaving the canonical behavior undocumented at its public surface.
SUMMARY: Overall verdict: the delta correctly retires the duplicated `"factory"` literal and routes parity through a single resolver, resolving the prior MAJOR and NIT; no blocker, language rule and default-on config/docs remain consistent. Top risks are verification gaps, not behavior changes: the delegated tenant resolution is unpinned by tests against the old project-first rule (endangering AC-3 evidence integrity), and code now imports `core.backlog` while control evidence still names `core/backlog_scope.py` as owner. Recommend a test fixing project-vs-scope priority plus reconciling the named SSOT owner before Gate 2.
